issues.legal_issue: A court may extend time to pay a court fee despite expiry of the time fixed by a peremptory procedural order stating that the appeal will stand dismissed for non-payment.
material_facts: The court directed the appellant to pay the deficit court fee within a fixed period and stated that the appeal would stand dismissed if payment was not made in time.

The appellant applied for an extension on the last day of the period, before it expired, but the application was heard after expiry and dismissed on the ground that the appeal had already stood dismissed.
The court later rejected further applications on the same ground without considering whether time could be extended.
issues.conclusion: The court retained power to extend the time notwithstanding the peremptory order and the expiry of the original period; the orders refusing to consider that power were erroneous.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 148 and 149 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, permit enlargement of time even after the period fixed has expired, and section 151 preserves the court’s inherent power to do justice. A peremptory procedural order, unlike a conditional decree, is in essence in terrorem and does not completely estop the court from considering events and circumstances arising within the time fixed. The court relied on Lachmi Narain Marwari v. Balmakund Marwari and referred to Latham v. Johnson.

rule.if: appeal_proceeding and court_fixed_time_for_court_fee and order_was_peremptory_procedural_order and request_for_extension

predicates.appeal_proceeding: The matter is an appeal in which the appellant must comply with a court-fixed requirement.
predicates.court_fixed_time_for_court_fee: The court set a period within which a party had to pay a court fee.
predicates.order_was_peremptory_procedural_order: The court stated that non-compliance within the period would result in dismissal, through a procedural order rather than a conditional decree.
predicates.request_for_extension: A party asked the court to enlarge the time for compliance.

issues.definition: When an appeal is subject to a court-fixed court-fee deadline imposed by a peremptory procedural order, a request for more time does not cease to be within the court’s power merely because the deadline has passed.

issues.legal_issue: Sufficient cause for non-payment of a deficit court fee warrants extending time where the party sought an extension before the deadline and the application was not considered on its merits.
material_facts: The appellant applied for an extension on the last day allowed for payment and offered to pay part of the deficit immediately, with the balance to follow.
The appellant stated that he was seriously ill and had been unable to raise a loan because the grain market had suddenly slumped and people were unable to advance money.
The application was rejected because the appeal was treated as already dismissed, rather than on an assessment of the reasons for non-payment.
The Supreme Court examined the application and affidavit and found sufficient cause for extending time.
issues.conclusion: The Court set aside the dismissal of the appeal and suit and granted the appellant further time to pay the deficit court fee.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 148 and 149 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, the court had ample power to enlarge time, and section 151 supplied inherent power to do justice. The court held that sufficient cause was made out on the application and affidavit; the relevant procedural orders did not prevent the court from considering that cause.

rule.if: appeal_from_dismissal_for_court_fee_nonpayment and extension_request_made_before_deadline and illness_impeded_payment and loan_unavailable_due_to_market_conditions and partial_payment_offered and sufficient_cause_found

predicates.appeal_from_dismissal_for_court_fee_nonp: The matter is an appeal from dismissal of a proceeding for failure to pay the required court fee.
predicates.extension_request_made_before_deadline: The party asked for more time before the court-fixed payment period expired.
predicates.illness_impeded_payment: The party’s serious illness contributed to the inability to make the payment.
predicates.loan_unavailable_due_to_market_condition: A sudden market downturn prevented the party from obtaining a loan.
predicates.partial_payment_offered: The party offered to pay part of the required amount immediately and the balance later.
predicates.sufficient_cause_found: The court examined the party’s evidence and found an adequate explanation for non-payment.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns dismissal for court-fee non-payment and the party timely seeks an extension, offers partial payment, and establishes that illness and inability to obtain a loan impeded payment, the court may extend time if it finds sufficient cause.
